html:
Baikonur Cosmodrome is the world's first and largest space launch site, on the steppe of southern Kazakhstan near the Syr Darya river. The Soviet Union began building it in 1955.

The site was chosen for its flat, empty land, a railway line, and its place far south in the Soviet Union, where the Earth's spin gives rockets a little extra push. It was named after a mining town hundreds of kilometres away, to confuse spies. The rocket designer Sergei Korolev and his team worked here.

Some of the great firsts of the space age started at Baikonur:

  • Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, in 1957.
  • Vostok 1, which carried Yuri Gagarin into orbit in 1961.
  • The Buran shuttle in 1988.

When the Soviet Union broke up, the cosmodrome ended up in independent Kazakhstan. Russia leases it, together with the town of Baikonur, and Russian crews still fly to the International Space Station from here.
sum: Baikonur Cosmodrome is the world's first and largest space launch site, on the steppe of southern Kazakhstan near the Syr Darya river. The Soviet Union began building it in 1955.
